t:
In this Act:
    (1) Appropriate congressional committees.—The term “appropriate congressional committees” means—
        (A) the Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate; 
        (B) the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate; 
        (C) the Committee on Foreign Affairs of the House of Representatives; and 
        (D) the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives.  
    (2) Evaluation.—The term “evaluation” means, with respect to a covered United States foreign assistance program, the systematic collection and analysis of information about the characteristics and outcomes of the program, including projects conducted under such program, as a basis for—
        (A) making judgments and evaluations regarding the program; 
        (B) improving program effectiveness; and 
        (C) informing decisions about current and future programming.  
    (3) Covered united states foreign assistance.—The term “covered United States foreign assistance” means assistance authorized under—
        (A) part I of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 (22 U.S.C. 2151 et seq.), except for—
            (i) title IV of chapter 2 of such part (relating to the Overseas Private Investment Corporation); and 
            (ii) chapter 3 of such part (relating to International Organizations and Programs);  
        (B) chapter 4 of part II of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 (22 U.S.C. 2346 et seq.; relating to Economic Support Fund); 
        (C) the Millennium Challenge Act of 2003 (22 U.S.C. 7701 et seq.); and 
        (D) the Food for Peace Act (7 U.S.C. 1721 et seq.).

fable.w: This is purely a definitions section, defining "appropriate congressional committees," "evaluation," and "covered United States foreign assistance." The tempting reading is that the references to congressional committees and to "informing decisions" signal a consultative process, but Congress is inside the federal government and the definition of evaluation describes internal analysis rather than any outside-party role. No public comment, hearing, advisory body, consultation with non-federal entities, rulemaking, or right to sue is created.
fable.s: informing decisions about current and future programming

qwen_block.w: This section consists entirely of definitions for terms used in the Act. It defines 'appropriate congressional committees' and 'evaluation' but does not mandate any consultation, public hearing, or advisory process involving parties outside the federal government. Congress is considered inside the federal government, and defining terms does not constitute participation.
qwen_block.s: (1) Appropriate congressional committees.—The term “appropriate congressional committees” means— (A) the Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate; (B) the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate; (C) the Committee on Foreign Affairs of the House of Representatives; and (D) the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives.

opus.w: This section only defines terms. The one body it names, the congressional committees, is inside the federal government, and the "evaluation" definition describes the government's own internal analysis with no outside party involved. Words like "evaluation" and "informing decisions" look procedural, but they bring no non-federal party into a federal decision, so this is not participation.

qwen_chat.w: This section provides definitions for terms used in the Act. The definition of 'evaluation' describes an internal government process of collecting and analyzing information to inform decisions, but it does not require consultation with or participation from people outside the federal government. The other definitions refer to congressional committees (inside the government) or types of foreign assistance. Therefore, there is no participation as defined.
qwen_chat.s: (2) Evaluation.—The term “evaluation” means, with respect to a covered United States foreign assistance program, the systematic collection and analysis of information about the characteristics and outcomes of the program, including projects conducted under such program, as a basis for— (A) making judgments and evaluations regarding the program; (B) improving program effectiveness; and (C) informing decisions about current and future programming.
qwen_chat.b:
Temptation: The word "evaluation" might imply a process involving external stakeholders or public input.
Resolution: The definition of "evaluation" provided in the text is purely internal to the government's management of foreign assistance programs ("systematic collection and analysis of information... as a basis for... informing decisions"). It does not mandate consultation with outside parties. Furthermore, the other definitions are for internal government entities (Congress) or types of funding. There is no requirement for public participation, advisory boards with outside members, or consultation with non-federal entities.
